roads.name: West Ham Lane
roads.alignmentEvidence: T13 retrace (October 2026): centreline re-read on the OS London five-foot (1:1056) 1893-96 mosaic, NLS layer os-london-five-foot-1893, zoom 18 (about 0.37 m per pixel) from the Police Station at (244,-880) to the junction with Church Street and Abbey Road at (394,-568), midway between the dotted kerb lines of the printed WEST HAM LANE (labels read along the street: 'HAM LANE' by the Police Station, 'WEST HAM LANE' by the Baptist Chapel, 'LANE' at (385,-615)), checked against the EPFL 1891-96 building footprints on both frontages. Read every 10-20 m in straightened map strips; kerb-to-kerb about 8-9.5 m, frontages 12-17 m apart. Estimated: 7 m modelled carriageway, paving. The former trace was read at the VIII.22/VIII.23 sheet join and lay 5-55 m west of the lane, south of Paul Street on the east frontage of Arthingworth Street (see t13Retrace.prior).

prior.alignmentEvidence: Street or lane centreline checked against the same source map as the housing envelopes. Corrects the previous independently approximated road layer. Name corrected October 2026 (was "Warton Road"): OS London five-foot 1893–96 mosaic (NLS os-london-five-foot-1893, zoom 18), crops centred on scene (260,-830) and (320,-680), prints "WEST HAM LANE" along this street at about (248,-868) and (365,-640); the EPFL OS text layer has "HAM" (235,-889), "LANE" (258,-859), "WEST" (352,-692) and "LANE" (386,-614). No WARTON label is printed on this street; WARTON ROAD is printed at (-744,-758)/(-688,-677), on Warton Road northern section. Estimated: the traced centreline lies about 5–50 m west of the printed carriageway (traced at the VIII.22 sheet edge; the lane straddles the VIII.23 join) and south of Paul Street runs over the Arthingworth Street east frontage; geometry not corrected.

roads.name: Abbey Road northern section
roads.alignmentEvidence: T13 retrace (October 2026): the southern 140 m of the former 'West Ham Lane' trace, re-read on the OS London five-foot (1:1056) 1893-96 mosaic, NLS layer os-london-five-foot-1893, zoom 18 (about 0.37 m per pixel) where the street is printed 'ABBEY ROAD' (letters 'R O A D' at (381,-536)-(359,-493), 'A B B E Y' southward to (334,-436)), midway between the dotted kerb lines. Starts one vertex inside West Ham Lane so the two corridors overlap through the junction. Estimated: 8 m carriageway, paving. The modelled Abbey Road further south (from (322,-372)) is a separate record and is not joined here.

roads.name: Arthingworth Street
roads.alignmentEvidence: T13 retrace (October 2026): added. ARTHINGWORTH STREET is printed on the OS London five-foot (1:1056) 1893-96 mosaic, NLS layer os-london-five-foot-1893, zoom 18 (about 0.37 m per pixel) at about (286,-690)-(320,-600), parallel to and about 40 m west of West Ham Lane, from Barnby Street to Skiers Street. Line first fitted midway between the EPFL 1891-96 footprint frontages, then moved 1.7 m east onto the midpoint of the dotted kerb lines read in straightened map strips at 40-100 m and 110-170 m along the street (kerb to kerb 8.0-8.1 m; the EPFL footprints sit about 1.5 m off the printed house fronts here). Measured: 8 m carriageway. Estimated: paving. Three east-return housing rows that had been fitted to the misplaced West Ham Lane trace front this street.

roads.name: Albion Street
roads.alignmentEvidence: T13 retrace (October 2026): re-read on the OS London five-foot (1:1056) 1893-96 mosaic, NLS layer os-london-five-foot-1893, zoom 18 (about 0.37 m per pixel) along the printed ALBION STREET ('ALBION' and 'STREET' at (-25,-698)-(25,-729)) from the Bridge Road centreline to the St Thomas Road centreline, midway between the EPFL footprint frontages (9.5-11.9 m apart). The former trace lay 8-12 m south-east, across the south frontage. Estimated: 6 m carriageway, paving.

RAILWAY PLACE is printed on the OS London five-foot (1:1056) 1893-96 mosaic, NLS layer os-london-five-foot-1893, zoom 18 (about 0.37 m per pixel) at (-51,-747)-(-23,-766) between Bridge Road and St Thomas Road. The south side is a continuous terrace built to the pavement line (EPFL footprints); the north side is yard walls and house ends about 4-5 m away. Centreline 2.6 m north of the south frontage. record.name: Angel Lane
record.alignmentEvidence: Street or lane centreline checked against the same source map as the housing envelopes. Corrects the previous independently approximated road layer. Name unverified, flagged October 2026: on the OS London five-foot 1893–96 mosaic (crop centred on scene (-30,-760)) and on the saved VIII.22 scan this trace crosses house plots in the block bounded by Bridge Road, Devon Terrace and Albion Street and follows no printed street; nearest printed names are RAILWAY PLACE, MOUNT PLACE, DEVON TERRACE and ALBION STREET. ANGEL LANE is printed about 600 m north, near scene (-72,-1357) (crop centred (-80,-1300)), with Angel Lane Bridge at (-77,-1482). Name left unchanged pending a geometry decision.
